message.content:
READ-ONLY IDOR audit of server actions in /opt/nxeon (Next.js, Prisma). I need you to check a set of "use server" action files for IDOR / missing-ownership bugs.

For EACH exported server action that takes an id/resourceId/xId string argument (the id comes from the untrusted client), determine whether the action verifies the resource belongs to the caller BEFORE reading or mutating it. The correct pattern is: after `requireUser()`, load the row and check `row.userId === user.id` (or team membership / `user.role === "ADMIN"`), throwing/returning on mismatch. Look especially for the ANTI-pattern: `db.MODEL.findUnique({where:{id}})` or `db.MODEL.update({where:{id},data})` / `db.MODEL.delete({where:{id}})` where the ONLY predicate is the client-supplied id and there is NO userId/ownership check — that is an IDOR (attacker passes another user's row id).

Also flag mass-assignment: an action that spreads untrusted input (`...input`, `...formData`, `data: input`) into a prisma create/update, especially if it could set `role`, `isAdmin`, `userId`, `balance`, `credits`, `status`, `plan`.

Files to audit (read each fully):
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-backup.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-sites.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-websites.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-ops.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-extra.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-disk.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-firewall.ts

Note: many files use a helper like `ownedServer(serverId)` / `ownedX(id)` that does the check — if an action routes through such a helper, it is SAFE, don't report it. Only report actions where the id-to-resource lookup has NO ownership predicate reachable by a normal customer.

For each real finding report: exact file:line, the action name, the model, what an attacker reads/mutates, and the one-line fix. Rank CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM. If a file is clean, say so in one line. Be precise and avoid false positives — verify the helper actually checks ownership before calling it clean. Return findings as your final message text.

content.text:
I've read all 15 files fully and traced every exported server action to its ownership check. Here is the audit result.

## Summary: No IDOR or mass-assignment findings. All 15 files are clean.

Every exported action that takes a client-supplied `id`/`serverId`/`domainId`/`volumeId`/`ruleId` routes its resource lookup through an ownership-checking helper (or an inline check) that runs after `requireUser()` and verifies `row.userId === user.id` (with an `ADMIN` bypass, which the prompt accepts). I verified each helper actually performs the check before the resource is read/mutated — none are decorative.

### Ownership helpers verified (all check `userId` before returning the row)
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts:410` `ownedDomain` — `domain.userId !== user.id && role !== ADMIN` (also inline checks at :300, :401 for `renewDomainAction`, `toggleDomainAutoRenew`; `purchaseDomain` looks up by unique `name` and checks `existing.userId` at :150).
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:62` `ownedDomain` / `:70` `ownedActiveDomain` — every redirect/lock/bulk-DNS action goes through these. `parseDnsImport` is a pure text parser (no DB, no id) so it's not an IDOR surface.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:51` `ownedDomain` — used by `updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts` — `quoteTransferIn`/`submitTransferIn` check `existing.userId` on the unique-name lookup (:85, :178); `cancelTransferIn` checks at :363.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts:57` `ownedServer` (selects `userId`, checks at :72) — every file-manager action wraps it.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-backup.ts:25` `ownedServer`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:37` `ownedVolume` + `:45` `ownedServer` — `attachVolume` checks BOTH the volume and the target server; the private `volumePriceCents` is correctly not exported.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-disk.ts:29` `ownedServer`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-sites.ts:58` `ownedSite` (`site.userId !== user.id`, no admin bypass — stricter).
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-websites.ts:41` `ownedServer` + `:52` `ownedWebsite` (checks the Website's own `userId`); `toggleWebsite`/`requestWebsiteSsl`/`deleteWebsite` mutate `where:{id}` using the same id already ownership-verified.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server.ts:13` `ownedServer`; `deletePortForward` uses `deleteMany({where:{id, serverId}})` scoped to the owned server.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-ops.ts:15` `ownedServer`; `requestRestore` additionally validates the `volid` against `listBackups(server.vmid)` (:134), preventing cross-tenant restore-by-guess.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:20` `ownedServer`. `osTemplateId`/`newPlanId` lookups are catalog rows (not user-scoped), so no ownership applies.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-extra.ts:7` `ownedServer`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-firewall.ts:21` `ownedServer`; `toggleFirewallRule` uses `findFirst({where:{id:ruleId, serverId}})`, `deleteFirewallRule` uses `deleteMany({where:{id, serverId}})`, and `reorderFirewallRules` filters ids to the server's own rule set (:132-134) — all rule access is scoped to the ownership-checked server.

### Anti-patterns specifically checked for and NOT present
- No `db.MODEL.findUnique/update/delete({where:{id}})` reachable by a customer where the client id is the only predicate and ownership is unchecked. Every such call is preceded by an ownership-verified load of that same id, or scoped by a `serverId`/`userId` predicate on an already-owned parent.
- No mass-assignment: no action spreads `...input`/`...formData` or passes `data: input` into a Prisma create/update. Every `data:` object is explicitly field-listed; `role`/`isAdmin`/`userId`/`balanceCents`/`credits`/`status`/`plan` are never set from untrusted input (`userId` is always set to `user.id`, statuses to server-side literals).
- Ownership predicates all use the correct `&&` composition (`userId !== user.id && role !== "ADMIN"`) — no `||` inversion bug.

No findings to rank. If you have adjacent `"use server"` files (e.g. `lib/actions.ts`, admin actions, or IP/DNS-token actions) outside this list, I can extend the audit to those.
